title: Representables of w-contractible affines are projective
statement:
Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$ with $D$ w-contractible be an object of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$.

1. Every epimorphism of sheaves of sets $F\to h_U$ has a section.
2. $h_U$ is projective in $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}})$: for every epimorphism $F\to G$, the map
   $F(U)\to G(U)$ is surjective.

proof.text: By [det-pe-topos-functoriality-site], $h_U=\operatorname{Hom}_X(-,U)$ is a sheaf. Let $\varphi:F\to h_U$ be an epimorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective] to $\mathrm{id}_U\in h_U(U)$. It gives a covering $\{u_i:U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ and $a_i\in F(U_i)$ such that $\varphi_{U_i}(a_i)=u_i$ for each $i$. This is local surjectivity in sheaves of sets, with no assumption that $\varphi_U$ is already surjective.

source.place: opening sentence and part 1, local lifts of the identity; Stacks sites.tex Tag 00WN, lemma-mono-epi-sheaves

proof.text: Apply [det-pe-wcb-clopen-partition] to this covering of the affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$, using precisely the assumed w-contractibility of $D$. Obtain a finite clopen partition $U=\bigsqcup_{k=1}^m U_k^\prime$ and $U$-morphisms $g_k:U_k^\prime\to U_{i_k}$. Write $j_k:U_k^\prime\hookrightarrow U$ for the inclusions and put $b_k=F(g_k)(a_{i_k})$. Naturality gives $\varphi_{U_k^\prime}(b_k)=u_{i_k}\circ g_k=j_k$. No lift into a single member of the original covering is asserted.

source.place: part 1, clopen refinement and restrictions of the lifts; Stacks proetale.tex Tag 098F, lemma-w-contractible-proetale-cover

proof.text: The inclusions $j_k$ form a Zariski covering, hence a pro-étale covering by the explicit Zariski-cover clause of [sk-def-pe-site]. In particular the pieces and their intersections are objects of this site. For any sheaf of sets $H$, the empty covering of the empty scheme is a covering by the finite-refinement covering definition, so the sheaf equalizer condition of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] makes $H(\varnothing)$ a singleton. Thus for $k\ne l$ the restrictions of $b_k$ and $b_l$ to $U_k^\prime\times_U U_l^\prime=\varnothing$ agree; for $k=l$ the fibre product is $U_k^\prime$ and the two restrictions are identical. The same sheaf equalizer condition glues these sections uniquely to $b\in F(U)$. The sections $\varphi_U(b)$ and $\mathrm{id}_U$ restrict to $j_k$ on every piece, so separatedness of $h_U$ gives $\varphi_U(b)=\mathrm{id}_U$. For $U=\varnothing$ the same reasoning uses the empty partition and the unique empty matching family.

source.place: part 1, disjointness, gluing and equality with the identity; Stacks proetale.tex Tag 098B, lemma-etale-proetale, and sites.tex sheaf equalizer definition

proof.text: Apply [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] to the category $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and the underlying presheaf of $F$. The section $b$ corresponds to a natural transformation $s:h_U\to F$, explicitly $s_V(t)=F(t)(b)$ for $t:V\to U$. Since sheaves form a full subcategory of presheaves, it is a sheaf morphism. Naturality of $\varphi$ and $\varphi_U(b)=\mathrm{id}_U$ give $\varphi_V(s_V(t))=h_U(t)(\mathrm{id}_U)=t$ for every $V,t$. Hence $\varphi\circ s=\mathrm{id}_{h_U}$, proving clause 1.

source.place: end of part 1, Yoneda and the section; Stacks categories.tex Tag 001P, lemma-yoneda

proof.text: For clause 2 let $\alpha:F\to G$ be any epimorphism and let $y\in G(U)$. By [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] it determines a sheaf map $\eta:h_U\to G$ with $\eta_V(t)=G(t)(y)$. Define the pullback sheaf explicitly by $P(V)=\{(x,t)\in F(V)\times h_U(V):\alpha_V(x)=G(t)(y)\}$, with coordinatewise restrictions. It is a sheaf: glue the two coordinates by the sheaf equalizer condition of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; the displayed equality holds on the glued coordinates because it holds after restriction to each member of the cover and $G$ is separated. The projection $p:P\to h_U$ is locally surjective: for $t\in h_U(V)$, local surjectivity of $\alpha$ from [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective], applied to $G(t)(y)$, gives locally sections $x_i$ with $\alpha(x_i)=G(t|_{V_i})(y)$, so $(x_i,t|_{V_i})$ lifts $t|_{V_i}$. The converse direction of that same node makes $p$ an epimorphism. This proves the particular stability of epimorphisms under pullback used here directly from its local-lifting criterion.

source.place: part 2, pull back the epimorphism along the map represented by y; explicit verification of the topos assertion

proof.text: Apply clause 1, already proved in steps 1–4, to the epimorphism $p:P\to h_U$. Its section $r$ yields $r_U(\mathrm{id}_U)=(x,\mathrm{id}_U)$ for some $x\in F(U)$. The defining equality for $P(U)$ says $\alpha_U(x)=G(\mathrm{id}_U)(y)=y$. Thus $F(U)\to G(U)$ is surjective for every epimorphism. Under the natural Yoneda bijections of [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection], this is exactly the lifting property of $h_U$ against epimorphisms, hence its projectivity, proving clause 2.

source.place: end of part 2, section of the pullback and projection to F

proof_origin.place: parts 1 and 2, with local-surjectivity, Yoneda and the pullback argument made explicit
